action.description: Action object MUST contain a field `submission`, and MAY contain arbitrary additional information.

actTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) to obtain an action from an agent.

episodeSteps.description: Maximum number of steps in the episode.

includeLegalActions.description: If true, include legalActions and legalActionStrings in observations. Defaults to false since these can be derived from serializedGameAndState.

initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameName.description: The short_name of the OpenSpiel game to load.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

savePrompt.description: If true, the LLM prompt produced by the harness is included as a 'prompt' field on the action returned by core_harness, which causes it to be persisted in the episode replay. Defaults to false to keep replays small.

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

strictMode.description: If true, agents must return only {'submission': int} (no extra fields like 'thoughts'), and per-agent TIMEOUT/ERROR/INVALID counts as a loss for the offending agent only — other agents win. If false (default), any agent error halts and voids the entire episode, matching the lenient research-mode behavior.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

No immediate threats or wins are possible for either side. Column 3 is blocked for vertical connectivity by the intervening O, so returning there would isolate our existing bottom X and create an alternating stack that neither player is likely to continue filling. 

Instead, the optimal strategy is to build connectivity with our existing bottom X by playing adjacent to it. This creates a strong base for future horizontal lines along the bottom row and opens a powerful diagonal line (row 5/col 3 to row 4/col 4 to row 3/col 5 to row 2/col 6). Columns 2 and 4 are symmetric and equally strong here, but column 4 is selected without loss of generality. Columns farther from the center (0, 1, 5, 6) are suboptimal as they offer fewer connecting lines overall.

The single existing 'o' disk is centrally located. Dropping in column 4 will place the new 'o' disk directly adjacent to it (horizontal connection at row 4, columns 3-4). This is a strong developing move that:
- Prioritizes the center (columns 3-4 are the most strategically valuable).
- Creates multiple setup options for future lines (horizontal extensions, diagonals with the new disk, or vertical in column 4).
- Responds to the adjacent 'x' disks at the bottom without ceding central control or allowing easy opponent threats on the next turn.

Moves in columns 2 or 3 are reasonable alternatives (also connecting to the existing 'o'), but column 4 best balances central influence, connectivity, and flexibility without stacking higher in an already-occupied column.

action.thoughts:
The current board has X pieces at the bottom of columns 3 and 4, with O pieces directly above them in row 4 of those same columns. All other positions are empty. No player has an immediate win or even a 3-in-a-row yet.

Playing in column 5 drops an X into row 5 of column 5. This creates three consecutive X pieces horizontally along the bottom (columns 3-5). This move creates two separate winning threats on the next turn:
- Column 2 (row 5) would complete four X pieces in columns 2-5.
- Column 6 (row 5) would complete four X pieces in columns 3-6.

O has only one move and can block at most one of these threats (by playing in column 2 or 6). Whichever threat O blocks, X can take the other on the subsequent turn to complete a horizontal 4-in-a-row and win immediately. O has no way to create an immediate win or double threat of their own on this turn (they only have two pieces total), so they cannot win before X does. If O fails to block either threat, X wins even sooner by claiming one of the open winning spots.

The position is symmetric, so column 2 produces an identical forced win by creating three bottom X pieces (columns 2-4) with threats at columns 1 and 5. Other moves (such as columns 0, 1, 3, 4, or 6) do not create double threats and allow O to respond effectively.

Thus, column 2 is an optimal move.

Final Answer: 2
